speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an infant with recurrent stridor and wheezing; to begin our evaluation, can you describe exactly when these symptoms occur, such as during feeding, crying, or lying down?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with associated Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).

The symptoms of inspiratory stridor, worsening with crying and neck flexion, alongside post-prandial vomiting, are classic presentations for this condition. I will recommend an Upper GI series with fluoroscopy to evaluate for reflux and confirm the diagnosis.
